text.p: The London Metals Exchange was closed on Monday and will reopen on Tuesday, May 6.
In Chicago, the Commodities Research Bureau index fell 0.28 points to 246.34.

COMEX and NYMEX precious metals futures ended higher Monday, on light volumes, with activity dampened by the U.K. bank holiday and the Golden Week holidays in Tokyo. "In gold there was some fund shortcovering early and some bullion bank buying in a quiet market near the close, but, after finding support around $340 last week, June gold really needs to get above $345.20 to break out of the recent downtrend," North American Equity Services trader, John Geraghty, said. COMEX June gold ended up $2.70 an ounce at $344.30, after seeing a five day high at $344.80 early. In the bullion market, spot gold ended quoted $342.50/00, compared with the New York close Friday around $339.95/45.

CBOT wheat futures closed lower amid growing bearish sentiment on technicals and improving crop prospects in the U.S., Australia and Europe, although commercial buying limited losses, floor sources said. "Wheat had a fairly important technical breakdown," said Dave Armstrong, analyst with ABN-AMRO Chicago Corp. "It closed below the post-freeze low of $4.14 (on the July contract)." July finished 5-1/4 cents a bushel lower at $4.11-1/4.

NYMEX crude prices ended modestly higher Monday, paring larger gains made early session on technical strength and news ethnic clashes in Nigeria continued to disrupt oil production there. June crude ended up three cents at $19.63 a barrel after rising as high as $19.88 before late profit-taking set in. The closure of London's IPE due to a U.K. holiday thinned trade. "Today was a wash. At the end, local players picked each others' pockets, and we ended near unchanged which is better since we can have a real day tomorrow when London is open," said a New York crude dealer.
